subject: parallel Processing in BioGeoBEARS not using all cores

messages.author: a65abcf2d8c47b08
messages.subject: parallel Processing in BioGeoBEARS not using all cores
parts:
Hi there. 

I have a issue in trying to run BioGeoBEARS in all cores of my PC. I have set the Parallel package correctly and used detectCores() in the $num_cores_to_use (I currently have 16 cores). The analysis run without error, but I realised tha my PC is not using all cores, just one in 100%. I've searched online and saw that parallel uses mcapply, and so do BioGeoBEARS, but i could not put it to work. Any ideias on how to use all cores in the PC?

Cheers!!

messages.author: 115d05260b0c341a
messages.subject: Re: [BioGeoBEARS] parallel Processing in BioGeoBEARS not using all cores
parts:
Hi -- I'm not sure about this one.  I know that R.app, on Macs, will not run parallel processes even if they are otherwise correctly set up -- you have to run them in the base R command prompt. 

On a windows PC (I assume you have this), it is possible there is something similar going on in e.g. Rstudio or whatever.  I would say, try it in the R command prompt (i.e. typing "R.exe" or whatever it is at the windows command prompt), then try to run some of the mclapply examples and see if they work.  All BioGeoBEARS does is use this pre-existing machinery, so if that machinery doesn't work on a particular platform, I have no special knowledge...

Cheers!
Nick

Hi there, thanks for the quick feedback.

So, i'm running R in a Debian (Linux) system, and tried lot of things. First, I ran in the RStudio. Then I openned the terminal and ran from there. Both of the runs showed the same result: one core usage at 100%.

I'm currently runing like this:

if (runslow)
{
  res = mclapply(BioGeoBEARS_run_object, bears_optim_run(BioGeoBEARS_run_object), mc.cores = detectCores()) 
  res    
  
  save(res, file=resfn)
  resDEC = res
} else {
  # Loads to "res"
  load(resfn)
  resDEC = res
}

I don't know if the sintax is correct for the mclapply() function or even if this makes any sense (Im very very new in the parallel processing side of R, so i beg your pardon if this doenst make sense haha), but surprisingly it is running **something** and not outputing nothing, but all my cores are been used. Could it mean something?

Thanks a lot!
Cheers.
